summary.interpretation: Semantic ontology overlap maps PC concept labels from both corpora into the FrontierGraph ontology before comparing retained PC neighborhoods. This is stricter than the current family overlap and less brittle than raw label overlap. It still inherits the quality of the extraction-label mapping and should be audited before becoming a substantive result.

families.product_evidence: Reference asset; option package; cap/buffer or floor rule; fixed outcome period.
families.academic_evidence: Portfolio insurance / structured product / downside-protection mechanism rather than exact ETF wrapper.
families.nearest_academic_object: Equilibrium Analysis of Portfolio Insurance: portfolio insurance --same payoff-protection rationale--> buffer-defined outcome strategy
families.reason: The products use FLEX options to deliver capped upside with downside protection, which is closest to portfolio insurance rather than a distinct named strategy match.
families.caveat: The academic candidates discuss portfolio insurance in general, not the exact ETF wrapper, benchmark, or outcome-period mechanics.

families.product_evidence: Income objective; call-option writing; equity/high-dividend exposure; benchmarked against equity and fixed-income indexes.
families.academic_evidence: Buy-write / covered-call strategy; option-income tradeoff; empirical performance of covered-call indexes.
families.nearest_academic_object: The efficiency of the buy-write strategy: Evidence from Australia: CBOE S&P 500 BuyWrite Index --same_strategy--> covered call income / buy-write strategy
families.reason: The product explicitly uses covered calls on equities for income and lower volatility, which is the same operational strategy as buy-write/covered-call writing studied in the academic candidate.
families.caveat: The academic candidates are framed around buy-write indices and empirical performance, while the product is a fund implementation on dividend-paying equities.

families.product_evidence: Lifecycle asset allocation; underlying funds; target retirement date; glide-path rule.
families.academic_evidence: Target-date funds; lifecycle portfolio allocation; glide-path and investor retirement horizon.
families.nearest_academic_object: Retail Financial Innovation and Stock Market Dynamics: The Case of Target Date Funds: target date fund --same_strategy--> target date lifecycle fund
families.reason: The products are target-date lifecycle funds with glide-path asset allocation and fund-of-funds implementation, matching the academic target date fund counterpart directly.

families.product_evidence: Crypto futures or futures-linked exposure; sometimes paired with volatility management, alternatives, or macro sleeves.
families.academic_evidence: Bridge is mechanism-level and strongest where product graph explicitly contains bitcoin/crypto futures.
families.nearest_academic_object: Price volatilities of bitcoin futures: Stochastic investment model --prediction--> Bitcoin futures
families.reason: The closest academic match is the bitcoin-futures literature, which shares the same exposure mechanism through futures-based crypto access, even though the product family also includes broader fintech equity exposure and trust-based wrappers.
families.caveat: The family is heterogeneous, so the match fits the bitcoin-futures subset better than the full set of products.

families.product_evidence: Crypto/digital-asset reference exposure; sometimes equity or treasury-company wrapper; often option-income overlay.
families.academic_evidence: Bridge is mechanism-level: academic finance studies crypto exposure, pricing, and futures mechanisms more directly than product wrappers.
families.nearest_academic_object: Price volatilities of bitcoin futures: Stochastic investment model --prediction--> Bitcoin futures
families.reason: The closest academic match is the bitcoin-futures literature, which shares the same exposure mechanism through futures-based crypto access, even though the product family also includes broader fintech equity exposure and trust-based wrappers.
families.caveat: The family is heterogeneous, so the match fits the bitcoin-futures subset better than the full set of products.

families.product_evidence: Stock-selection products using quality, profitability, growth, value, or sustainability screens.
families.academic_evidence: Bridge improved after retrieval fix: product quality/growth screens align with quality-investing and quality-premium rationales.
families.nearest_academic_object: Quest for a parsimonious factor model in the wake of quality-minus-junk, misvaluation and Fama-French-six factors: Quality investing --relationship--> quality premium / quality-minus-junk
families.reason: The product explicitly targets high-quality companies and management/business-model quality, which aligns with the academic quality-investing or quality-minus-junk rationale.
families.caveat: The fund also layers in sustainable-growth and ESG screening, so the match is not a pure standalone quality factor strategy.

families.product_evidence: Factor or allocation products where volatility, risk control, or economic-cycle state changes affect exposure.
families.academic_evidence: Bridge is mechanism-level: products use target-volatility or risk-control logic, but family remains heterogeneous.
families.nearest_academic_object: False Safe Haven Assets: Evidence From the Target Volatility Strategy Based on Recurrent Neural Network --target-volatility / volatility-control portfolio rule--> managed volatility overlay
families.reason: The products use managed risk or managed volatility overlays, which is closest to the academic target-volatility control rule among the retrieved candidates.
families.caveat: The match is mechanism-level only; the retrieved papers do not directly map to the specific fund structures or commodity trend-following overlay.
